page: Amazon Web Services m8g.4xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. Operating on the arm64 architecture, it features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz, with one thread per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance runs on the Nitro hypervisor, does not include any local storage, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps. There are no bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark testing, the m8g.4xlarge demonstrates strong memory and decompression capabilities. Its Passmark memory score ranks in the top tier, supported by strong large-block memory bandwidth of 296.67 GB/sec for read-only and 133.88 GB/sec for write operations. Single-threaded and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performance also rank in the top 25 percent, alongside database operations. Most general compute benchmarks, including stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, Geekbench scores, and Redis SET operations, fall within the average range. However, the server exhibits weaker performance in prompt processing for medium-sized LLM models, which registers in the bottom 25 percent.

The ARMv9 architecture offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading. However, the lack of local storage requires external network storage attachments, and the absence of a GPU limits its utility for heavy parallel processing or large-scale AI training. The instance is suited for general-purpose workloads, including database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and lightweight text or image processing.
